content_html:
Preparing your backpack well for Machu Picchu can make the difference between a smooth experience… or an uncomfortable day.

It’s not about bringing more things.
It’s about bringing the right things.

Why is it important to know what to bring to Machu Picchu?

Machu Picchu is a hike in a natural environment.

This means:

  • Constant weather changes
  • Long walking routes
  • Limited access to shops inside the site

If you forget something important, you won’t be able to fix it easily.

Checklist: what to bring in your backpack for Machu Picchu

Essentials:

  • Passport or ID
  • Machu Picchu ticket (digital or printed)
  • Cash (Peruvian soles)

For the weather:

  • Waterproof jacket or rain poncho
  • Cap or hat
  • Sunglasses
  • Sunscreen

Hydration and energy:

  • Reusable water bottle
  • Light snacks (nuts, energy bars, fruit)

Comfort during the visit:

  • Small backpack (no larger than 20L)
  • Camera or phone with a full battery
  • Power bank (portable charger)
  • Wet wipes or toilet paper

Recommended extras:

  • Insect repellent
  • A light change of clothes (optional)
  • Plastic bags (to protect your belongings from rain)

Key tip: be prepared for rain

Even during the dry season, it can rain.

That’s why:

  • Always bring a waterproof jacket
  • Protect your backpack with a cover or bag

Rain can appear at any moment.

What NOT to bring to Machu Picchu

To avoid issues at the entrance:

Avoid bringing:

  • Large backpacks (not allowed)
  • Unnecessary heavy items
  • Drones (restricted)
  • Walking sticks without rubber tips

Common traveler mistake

Many people bring too much… or too little.

Result:

  • They get tired faster
  • They forget essentials
  • They don’t enjoy the experience

The key is balance: light, but complete.

Travel prepared and enjoy to the fullest

Having the right backpack allows you to:

  • Walk comfortably
  • Enjoy the route without stress
  • Adapt to the weather
  • Have a better overall experience
